liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Sugaree** (2 reviews): Reviewer finds Sugaree incredible, with the band sustaining high energy afterward; Reviewer has never heard Jerry stretch out on Sugaree like this [24][25]
- **Candyman** (1 other source): The start of Candyman was patched in from the audience source [4]
- **Lazy Lightning** (1 review): Jerry's playing on Lazy Lightning is fast and energetic, far from lazy [27]

## Setlist highlights

- **Billy for President**: mythic rare: 2 archived performances [28]

## The recordings

- **gd80-06-21.sbd.clugston.8639.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 23 songs; 172 min; rated 4.53/5 by 32 [1]. Said about its sound: Matrix recording has a few flaws, though the performance is strong [22]
- **gd1980-06-21.sbd.clugston.tetzeli.fix-8639.74407.reflac.flac16**: soundboard; 23 songs; 174 min [4]
- **gd1980-06-21.156398.mtx.photoleon.t-flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 22 songs; 174 min [5]
- **gd80-06-21.akg.vernon.23531.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 22 songs; 170 min; rated 4.56/5 by 16 [6]. Said about its sound: Audience recording sounds acceptable, considering the likely difficult recording conditions; Audience tape is crisp, with plenty of room ambiance and strong low end; among the best-sounding audience recordings in the reviewer's collection; Audience recording sparkles; reviewer rates sound five stars, playing four, same as the 6/20 show [16][20][23][27]
- **gd1980-06-21.144909.nak700.severson.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 22 songs; 174 min [7]

## Around the show

- Third consecutive night at West High Auditorium; announcements called it Anchorage's only concert hall and asked the crowd not to smoke to protect it [16]
- Reviewer says the band was tight and energetic, with Jerry giving an outpouring on guitar and vocals [21]
- Reviewer judges this the best show of the Anchorage run [20]
- Reviewer gives this show the same sound rating as the 6/20 show [23]
- Reviewer likes all three Anchorage shows but ranks this one the best [24]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd80-06-21.sbd.clugston.8639.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Mentions a Bertha remaster and a possible Gans version of the show as other circulating sources; Soundboard master went from cassette to reel to DAT to CDR, with an audience cassette as secondary source; AKG 414 audience source supplies the announcements, the opening of Sugaree, and part of Loser [1][26]
- **gd1980-06-21.sbd.clugston.tetzeli.fix-8639.74407.reflac.flac16**: transferred by Scott Clugston and Bill Tetzeli; source: Master Soundboard Cassette > Reel To Reel > DAT> CDR [4]. Also: Bill redid the audience patches, matching pitch and volume to the soundboard, using 4-5 second crossfades; Patch material came from Eddie Claridge's audience recording, taken from Healy's AKG 414 stereo microphone [4]
- **gd1980-06-21.156398.mtx.photoleon.t-flac16**: source: Matrix created in Adobe Audition by Joe Noel [5]. Also: Matrix uses Mark Severson's front-of-board recording, mastered by Scott Clugston, with cassettes transferred by David Gans; Soundboard cassette masters shared by Richard Hale; Charlie Miller handled transfer and processing [5]
- **gd80-06-21.akg.vernon.23531.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Eddie Claridge patching from Dan Healy; source: Audience Recording: AKG 414 stereo mic [6]. Also: The soundboard version opens with an audience patch in Sugaree; reviewer prefers the audience tape taped by Eddie Claridge [23]
- **gd1980-06-21.144909.nak700.severson.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Mark Severson; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Mark Severson's Master Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 700 mics (mounted on pole, right center, Row M Seat 2) > Sony TC-D5 (Maxell XLII) [7]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead West High Auditorium - June 21, 1980](https://www.dead.net/show/june-21-1980) [29]
- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Jerry @ West High Auditorium, June 21, 1980](https://www.dead.net/fanphotos/jerry-west-high-auditorium-june-21-1980) [30]
